articles.title: 206 sign-in starts, 0 signups: the denominator was fake. A 12-line counter for static sites.
articles.excerpt: A founder posted a funnel last week that looked catastrophically broken. Seven days, 206 sign-in starts, 0 completed signups. Numbers like that send you straight into the auth code. The code was fine.…
articles.body: A founder posted a funnel last week that looked catastrophically broken. Seven days, 206 sign-in starts, 0 completed signups. Numbers like that send you straight into the auth code. The code was fine. Of 205 clicks on the Google sign-in button over four days, about 190 came from a single country, every session a brand new visitor, and many reporting browser and OS pairs that do not ship in the real world. Safari on Linux is a user-agent string someone typed. Once that traffic was excluded, seven-day visitors dropped from 358 to about 85, and sign-in starts dropped from 206 to 1. The one remaining start was the founder's own test. Nothing in the funnel was broken. The denominator was.

articles.title: How OBJ to STL conversion works in the browser (no server needed)
articles.excerpt: I built objtostl.com, a free converter that turns a Wavefront OBJ file into an STL for 3D printing. The whole conversion happens in the browser tab. Here's how that works, and the things that go wrong…
articles.body: I built objtostl.com , a free converter that turns a Wavefront OBJ file into an STL for 3D printing. The whole conversion happens in the browser tab. Here's how that works, and the things that go wrong if you skip them. The two formats OBJ is a text format. The lines that matter for printing look like this: v 0.0 0.0 0.0 # vertex position v 1.0 0.0 0.0 v 1.0 1.0 0.0 f 1 2 3 # face, 1-based vertex indices Faces can have more than three vertices, indices can be negative (relative to the end of the list so far), and a face entry can carry texture and normal indices ( f 1/1/1 2/2/2 3/3/3 ). OBJ files often reference an .mtl material file too. STL is much simpler: a flat list of triangles.

articles.title: AI Made Hacking Cheaper. Here's How to Defend Your Website.
articles.excerpt: One operator. More than 1,200 websites attempted. An estimated $5,000 in AI usage. On 19 October, Reuters reported that one hacker had used AI agents to break into websites belonging to more than 100…
articles.body: One operator. More than 1,200 websites attempted. An estimated $5,000 in AI usage. On 19 October, Reuters reported that one hacker had used AI agents to break into websites belonging to more than 100 companies. The AI bill of roughly $5,000 is the estimate of Snorre Fagerland, the NorForge researcher who uncovered the activity. Nothing about the requests themselves gave the AI away. They reached the same login forms, APIs and web servers any attacker uses. What changes is the work between those requests. An agent can read a response, revise its hypothesis, write a small program, record what it learned and choose another test. An operator can leave several investigations running while concentrating on the ones that produce access.

articles.title: Counting, Not Scrolling: A Formula-First Workflow for Amazon Review Mining
articles.excerpt: The graveyard Every Amazon seller I know has the same two files sitting somewhere: an export of a few hundred reviews nobody has time to read, and a Search Term Report that got downloaded, glanced at,…
articles.body: The graveyard Every Amazon seller I know has the same two files sitting somewhere: an export of a few hundred reviews nobody has time to read, and a Search Term Report that got downloaded, glanced at, and abandoned. There are SaaS tools that will happily charge $99+/month to fix this. What most of them do, underneath the dashboard, is show you your own data back with charts. The data was never the problem. The counting is the problem — and counting is free. So here's the workflow I run instead: a spreadsheet that counts, and one AI prompt that explains. In that order. Counting first, AI second Review mining is a counting problem before it's an AI problem. Paste 200 reviews into a chatbot and ask "what do buyers think?", and you get a summary that sounds plausible and ranks nothing.
articles.author: Prompt & Skill Co.

articles.title: Voice Agent Prompt Change Improved One Behavior but Broke Another
articles.excerpt: By Rokas Remeika. Published 4 October 2026. A system prompt change that improves one voice agent behavior will almost always trade away attention from another. You only see this trade if you measure t…
articles.body: By Rokas Remeika. Published 4 October 2026. A system prompt change that improves one voice agent behavior will almost always trade away attention from another. You only see this trade if you measure the untouched behavior in the same run, against a threshold written before you see the data. To stop regressions from reaching production, register a falsifier for every hypothesis before you run it: a specific metric that kills the change if it drops, regardless of how good the headline number looks. In my own environment, this pre-registered falsification forced me to revert three of my own prompt fixes before they shipped. Symptoms A system prompt change measurably improves the specific behavior you were targeting. The change ships to production because the headline metrics look positive.
articles.author: Rokas Remeika

articles.title: A 25-line check for botted crypto KOL accounts before you pay them
articles.excerpt: Paying a crypto KOL is mostly a bet on whether their audience is real. Follower counts are easy to fake. Engagement patterns are harder. We vet KOLs for a living, so here is the first-pass check we ru…
articles.body: Paying a crypto KOL is mostly a bet on whether their audience is real. Follower counts are easy to fake. Engagement patterns are harder. We vet KOLs for a living, so here is the first-pass check we run before anyone looks at a wallet or a rate card. It will not prove an account is clean. It tells you which accounts deserve a closer look. function kolRedFlags ( k ) { const flags = []; const engagement = k . avgLikes + k . avgReplies + k . avgReposts ; const er = engagement / k . followers ; if ( er < 0.002 ) flags . push ( ' engagement under 0.2% of followers ' ); if ( k . avgReplies / Math . max ( k . avgLikes , 1 ) < 0.01 ) flags . push ( ' almost no replies for the likes ' ); const growth = k . followers30dAgo ? ( k . followers - k . followers30dAgo ) / k .

articles.title: Could a $200K bond for satellites paid before launch prevent a space junk disaster in orbit? Here's why some scientists think so
articles.excerpt: The space around Earth is turning into a junkyard. Researchers think a refundable deposit scheme could force satellite operators to clean up their act before a tipping point is reached.
articles.body: The space around Earth is turning into a junkyard. Researchers think a refundable deposit scheme could force satellite operators to clean up their act before a tipping point is reached. For years, space sustainability experts have warned that the growing number of satellites in orbit and the quantity of dead metal left behind threatens to trigger a dangerous cascade of collisions known as the Kessler Syndrome . Predicted in the 1970s by NASA physicist Donald Kessler, this chain of orbital smashups could make the space around Earth unusable and unsafe. The dangerous tipping might be nearer than some think.

articles.body: God of War's Kratos almost went by a different name, but developers at Santa Monica Studio made too many Domino's pizza jokes. David Jaffe, the director of the original God of War trilogy, recently put out a video explaining the deep dish issue. Originally, Kratos was called “Dominus,” which Jaffe liked because it made him sound dominant and strong. Unfortunately, it also made him sound like a chain of pizza restaurants. “The people on the team started making Domino’s Pizza jokes,” Jaffe said . “Every single time someone said Dominus, someone inevitably would yell out, ‘30 minutes or free,’ or, ‘Get the door, it’s Dominus.’ “After about the 50th time, the writing was on the wall.

articles.title: NASA closes the book on epic OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission: 'I am immensely proud of what we did'
articles.excerpt: NASA's OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission formally ended on Sept. 30, 2026, though scientists will continue to study the pieces of space rock it returned for decades.
articles.body: On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth. The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu , an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks , the kind that may have seeded life on Earth. "I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn .

articles.body: _____________ THE PLACE Pyeongtaek, South Korea Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online. Construction of a fifth was halted during a drop in demand for memory chips in 2024 but restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring. articles.excerpt: 'More human than human. That's not a slogan; it's a shackle'
articles.body: Cue the depressing rain, dark trench coats, and a dire dystopian dirge because the Blade Runner 2099 trailer is here! Cyberpunk is charging back in confident fashion with Prime Video's latest detour into the neon-drenched dystopia of humans and rogue replicants first introduced in director Sir Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner" from 1982, then revisited in Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049." Arriving Nov. 25, 2026, " Blade Runner 2099" 's plot turns the tables as resentful artificial beings are now the ones running the show and hunting down Earth’s humans after a successful uprising against their original makers. This newest atmospheric trailer was unveiled at last week’s New York Comic-Con and has us totally jacked to re-immerse ourselves in that noirish futuristic realm.

articles.title: The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia
articles.excerpt: Brick by brick ... the truth is out there. You can now own a little piece of that with this 1,478-piece Lego set
articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.
